issues.claim: V09 §4.21.14 (4) (l.3651–3656) starts dust haze "where they give none — an arid row's dry weeks"; §3.16 row 93 (l.1612) gives "dust haze" as that edge's outcome; T-V9-87 (l.4322) asserts "dust haze in an arid row's dry weeks". V11 §3.25.11, the weather cells' home, rules otherwise: "a week with no live kind starts none" (V11 l.4645–4647), EI-V11-EDGE-6 "no spell comes, and Start a shower now starts none" (T-V11-48), and "a kind absent from a band stays absent through it (the arid dry months)". V11's arid row (l.4676) makes V09's example wrong both ways: in its dry weeks 13–38 the commonest live kind is heat shimmer (2 an hour, dust 1), and in weeks 0–9 and 50–51 no kind is live, so V09 would start a kind V11's band holds absent. V09's hand-off to V11 for the dust-haze case was not taken.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.14 (4) reads "It starts at once, as the timeline's next spell, the commonest live kind of the view's week (V11 §3.25.11's rule over the climate row's weather cells); in a week with no live kind it starts none, and the button is disabled with `settings.weather.noneThisWeek` ("No weather comes here this week."). It never starts snow on an `arid` row or on a row whose winter does not freeze (V11's compile rules hold the columns to it, and the button checks it again)." — the dust-haze clause deleted; §4.9's `settings.weather.<word>` row adds `noneThisWeek`; §3.16 row 93's outcome "dust haze" reads "the commonest live kind (heat shimmer in an arid row's dry weeks), or, with none live, the button disabled with `settings.weather.noneThisWeek`"; T-V9-87's "dust haze in an arid row's dry weeks" reads "heat shimmer in an arid row's dry weeks, and in a week with no live kind the button disabled with its line (V11 §3.25.11; T-V11-48)".

issues.claim: V09 §4.21.7 (2) (l.3369–3370): "A host's `view.set { week }` (§11.3) is a command, never an input (item 125 (c)): it moves the control as a user's pick does, turning the switch off" — with §3.16 row 94 (l.1613), T-V9-77 (l.4313: "a host's `view.set { week }` moves the control and turns the switch off") and J-V9.148 (l.4750). The base's homes say otherwise: §2.9's `week` (l.3297–3300) is item 67's drawn week, which "a host's `view.set { week }` sets … as a view command"; *The week's source* (l.3376–3377) calls it "a view command, as a user's scrub is"; `yearWeek`'s writers are V09's Season control and DR42 only (l.3330–3332), `seasonFollow` turns false on a user's "pick of a week or a season" (l.3341), "The `week` key … stays a different key … `yearWeek` is a look only" (l.3370–3371); and §11.3 (l.16278–16281) keeps `yearWeek` and `seasonFollow` among the per-viewer keys that never cross the bridge. V09's clause makes a host message write two per-viewer keys and flip the viewer's follow switch, against V09's own §4.21.7 (1) ("per viewer, never over a bridge").
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.7 (2)'s sentence reads "A host's `view.set { week }` (§11.3) is a command, never an input (item 125 (c)): it sets §2.9's `week` key — item 67's drawn week, which the Works and the crisis looks are read against — as a user's timeline scrub does, and never writes the year position or the follow switch, per-viewer keys no host message sets (§2.9, §11.3)."; §3.16 row 94's edge "a host's `view.set { week }` against a moved control" has the outcome "the drawn week moves; the Season control and its switch stay as the viewer left them"; T-V9-77's clause reads "a host's `view.set { week }` moves the drawn week and leaves the Season control and its switch unchanged (item 125 (c); §11.3)"; J-V9.148 drops "and to read a host's `view.set { week }` as a user's pick that turns the switch off".

issues.claim: A disaster look's units — V01's `disasterDistricts(doc, overlay, key)` (V01 §3.16), at the village rungs V07's units — have no reading in V09 (0 hits), though V09 uses them three times: §4.21.12 (4)'s `info.crisis.ruinedFor` on "a building in a district a disaster look ruins" (l.3580), §4.21.12 (5)'s **Show** "framing the look's camps" (l.3588–3589; a disaster look has no camps) and (7)'s **Go to**, "as the card's **Show** does". V01 names "volume 9's crisis card **Show** and Find's `crises` row" as consumers (V01 l.282) and states the frame — the union of the units' `FindArea` shapes (V01 §5.4 (6), l.3205–3210); V10 §2.13's `LookAnswer.crises.looks[].districts` (l.1010) reads them "as V09 §4.21.12 (4) reads them", a reading that section does not state, and CVR-V10-22 asks V09 for it.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.12 (4): "… a building in a district a disaster look ruins — one of the districts V01's `disasterDistricts(doc, overlay, key)` returns at `effectiveKey()` (V01 §3.16), at the village rungs V07's units — …"; (5): "**Show**, framing the look's place — its camps, or for a `disaster` look the union of its units' `FindArea` shapes (V01 §5.4 (6)) — as **Fit the town** frames the town"; §1b's crisis-lines row adds the input "V01's `disasterDistricts` for a disaster look's units (V01 §3.16)". V10 l.1010's citation and CVR-V10-22 then resolve.

issues.claim: V09 §4.21.13 (1) (l.3614–3616) gives the damage lines to "the plan panel … and the why card's `plan` section", and (3) (l.3629–3631) draws a disaster district's building's lines "at the look's `lookLevel` … under the head `info.crisis.ruinedFor`". The why card's sections are §11.2's `WhySection` rows (V09 §2.7), here V03 §4.6's `plan` provider, which carries the building's own level only — "A disaster's look is no row: the clerk tells it from the look read (V10 §3.9b (8)), and the panel shows it (V03 §4.5)" (V03 l.2384); V10 §3.9a and V10 §3.23 C10 ("the `plan` rows stay the building's own"); V03 §4.5 (l.2318–2322) puts the look's lines on the plan panel only. So the why card and the clerk would list different damage for one building, and T-V9-86's last clause ("volume 10's explanation of the same building renders the same keys", after the disaster clause) asserts the opposite of C10.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.13 (3) reads "In a district a disaster look ruins, the plan panel (V03 §4.5) shows the building's lines at the look's `lookLevel` by severity, or at its own level where that is higher, under the head `info.crisis.ruinedFor` — a look: nothing stored, ids and digests unchanged; the why card's `plan` section keeps the `plan` provider's rows at the building's own level (V03 §4.6), the look named by the card's `facts` row `info.crisis.ruinedFor` (V09 §4.21.12 (4)), as volume 10 tells it (V10 §3.9a; V10 §3.23 C10)."; T-V9-86's last clause reads "volume 10's explanation of each fixture building renders the same `info.damage.*` rows at the building's own level, and for the building in the disaster's district names the look by `info.crisis.*` (V10 §3.23 C10)".

issues.claim: Find at a drawn week whose frame is not the head (principle (11); V09's end of verify-rendering-r2t's VRC2T-07). V09 §4.21.10 (7) (l.3483) rebuilds the index "once per commit, regenerate, undo, redo, advance, load and migration, and at each `onEffectiveKey`" over §11.2's gazetteer listing, which answers over the head; (1) keeps the filter "through zoom, pan, band, layer, season, advance …" — never naming a change of §2.9's `week` (a timeline scrub, V09 §5.6; a host's `view.set { week }`). On a scrubbed past frame (V06 §3.15.2) the panel's counts, results, pins, ghost pins and gaps are undefined: by the text they glow, count and list buildings the frame does not hold. §3.16 rows 86–88 and T-V9-83 test no week change.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.10 (7)'s triggers add "each change of §2.9's `week` (a timeline scrub, a host's `view.set { week }`)", and (8) states: "At a drawn week whose frame is not the head (V06 §3.15.2), each chip's matches — its glow, pins, ghost pins, gaps, counts and results — are §11.2's listing restricted to the entities that frame holds: a match the frame lacks is neither drawn, pinned, counted nor listed, a chip with none there reads count 0 for that week (`find.none`), and the chips themselves are unchanged."; §3.16 row 87 adds the edge "a scrub to a week before a matched building was built, and after a closed use's end" with that outcome; T-V9-83 (e) adds the scrub; V10 §3.9b (7)'s `read_map find` reads the same restriction (the clerk counts what the panel shows). The base end (§8.2's *Find*, T-ER-25) is VRC2T-07's.
